portal_hypertension.title: Biopsy-Proven Hepatic Extramedullary Hematopoiesis With Chronic Portal Vein Thrombosis in JAK2 V617F-Positive Prefibrotic Myelofibrosis: Contributors to Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension.

portal_hypertension.abstract: Noncirrhotic portal hypertension warrants evaluation for vascular and infiltrative etiologies when hepatic fibrosis is absent. We describe a 48-year-old man with JAK2 V617F-positive prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis who developed chronic portal vein thrombosis with cavernous transformation and gastroesophageal varices despite preserved liver stiffness (4.2 kPa). Endoscopic ultrasound-guided liver biopsy demonstrated grade 2 hepatic extramedullary hematopoiesis (4 foci across 10 high-power fields) without fibrosis. Chronic portal vein thrombosis was the principal driver of portal hypertension. This case demonstrates that appreciable hepatic extramedullary hematopoiesis can occur in prefibroti...

portal_hypertension.abstract: Colonic variceal bleeding is a rare but potentially life-threatening manifestation of portal hypertension. Bevacizumab therapy is associated with an increased risk of variceal bleeding, but bleeding from ectopic varices is less well recognized. A 66-year-old man with alcohol-related cirrhosis and advanced hepatocellular carcinoma developed hematochezia on the day following the initiation of atezolizumab plus bevacizumab therapy. Acute ascending colonic variceal bleeding in the setting of portal hypertension and portal vein thrombosis. portal_hypertension.abstract: Liver dysfunction is a common complication in critically ill patients, and portal hypertension (PHT) represents a severe hepatic pathological condition closely associated with adverse patient outcomes. This study aims to investigate the impact of PHT on clinical outcomes in critically ill adult patients. Data were extracted from the Medical Information Market for Intensive Care IV database. All critically ill patients admitted to the hospital were included in this study.
